heroLead: New Salem sits in Fayette County's rolling farm country, close enough to the old Connellsville coke region that its mineral history often carries the same layered pattern.
intro: If your family's land near New Salem was ever part of the coal boom that shaped so much of Fayette County, there's a real chance oil and gas rights were handled separately from coal at some point in your deed history. Sorting that out takes actual title research rather than a guess based on what a neighbor's deed says.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Salem directly. We do that research through the county records ourselves and lay out exactly what we find before discussing any number.

sections.heading: Farm Country With a Coal Past
paragraphs: New Salem's surrounding farmland has generally stayed agricultural even as the coal and coke industry rose and fell around it, and Marcellus leasing has reached this part of Fayette County over the past decade or more. Wet-gas production here means both liquids revenue and processing deductions factor into your net royalty.
If your family's tract was part of a larger farm that got divided among heirs, your current decimal interest may be a fraction of what a grandparent originally held, which is common in this area.

sections.heading: Tracing a Fayette County Family Deed
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown, checking for any coal-era reservations and confirming the inheritance path that led to your current ownership.
This research takes real care in areas with this kind of layered history, and we do it before ever discussing an offer.

sections.heading: Reading Your Statement Honestly
paragraphs: We'll walk through your division order and any royalty statements with you so you understand your decimal interest, allocated production, and deductions clearly.

faqs.question: How do you check whether my family's coal and gas rights were separated?
faqs.answer: We research the recorded deed history for your specific parcel through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, checking for reservation language from the coal era.

faqs.question: My interest was split among several heirs. Is it still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Yes, small fractional interests from divided family farms are common in Fayette County, and we regularly buy interests of this kind.

faqs.question: Do you handle the transfer paperwork if we agree on a sale?
faqs.answer: Yes, we prepare and record the necessary transfer documents with the county recorder so you don't have to manage that process.
